sentences.text: Shri Basavaraj R. Math, learned counsel for appellants submitted that appeals were filed by claimants questioning dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.4 - insurer, challenging finding of tribunal insofar as contributory negligence and for enhancement of compensation.

3. It was submitted that on 09.04.2014, a Tempo bearing registration no.MH-04/GF-0368 was plying on Solapur - Pune Highway, when it dashed against Lorry bearing registration no.MH-42/M-4999 parked in middle of Highway without indicators or parking lights or taking any precaution.
Said accident resulted in death of three inmates of Tempo and grievous injuries upon two of them.

On separate claim petitions being filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, (for short 'M.V.
Act') against owner and insurer of Tempo and Lorry, respondents no.1 and 3 - owners of vehicles involved, did not appear and contest.
They were placed ex-parte.

Respondent no.2 - insurer of Lorry filed objections denying negligence of Lorry driver in causing accident on ground that it was safely parked on left side of road leaving sufficient room for movement of other vehicles.
It was contended that failure to stop Tempo before collision clearly established negligence on part of Tempo driver.

5. Respondent no.4 - insurer of Tempo contended that Tempo was goods carrying vehicle, therefore,
deceased and injured were unauthorized passengers and insurer was not liable to pay compensation.

Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence, wherein claimants were examined as PWs-1 to 4; Dr.S.S.Nagathan as PW-5 and marked - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6555 Exhibits-P1 to P23.
Two witnesses were examined by respondents and Exhibits-R1 to R5 were got marked.
7. On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to negligence of drivers of both vehicles, apportioned to extent of 60% against driver of Tempo and 40% against Lorry driver.
It assessed compensation and held owner/insurer of Lorry liable to pay 40% of compensation, while holding respondent no.3 - owner of Tempo liable to pay 60% of compensation.
Claim petition against respondent no.4 was dismissed.
8. Learned counsel for claimants submitted that admittedly accident occurred on Solapur - Pune Highway.
Accident spot sketch in Ex.P4 would indicate that there was service road on both sides of highway.
It was contended that Ex.P4 would clearly depict that offending Lorry was parked negligently on highway itself, blocking almost entire lane.
Admittedly, no precautionary measures were taken and none mentioned in police investigation - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6555 records.

It was contended that from Exs.P5 and P6 damages sustained by both vehicles would indicate attempt by driver of Tempo to avoid accident and that it occurred entirely due to negligent parking of Lorry on highway.
Further, Regulation 15 of Road Regulations prohibited parking of vehicle on road in unsafe manner.
Therefore, entire negligence for causing accident was that of Lorry driver and apportionment of negligence to extent of 60% on Tempo driver was not justified and required interference.

9. It was further submitted that when accident in question was due to negligence of drivers of both vehicles, as per ratio in decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Khenyei v/s New India Assurance Co. Ltd., reported in 2015 (9) SCC 273, claimants who had not contributed to cause of accident would be entitled to proceed and recover entire compensation from either of joint tort feasors.

15. On above grounds sought for allowing claimants' appeals.
16. Shri Sanjay M. Joshi, learned counsel for respondent no.2 - insurer of Lorry sought to justify award.
It was submitted that admittedly accident occurred in broad day light at 2:00 p.m.
Fact that driver of Tempo failed to stop vehicle before collision would indicate that he failed to maintain safe distance or failed to take adequate care and caution of other road users.

Further, driver of Lorry had stopped his vehicle on left side of road leaving - 16 - Sachin vs Sri.Dawood And Ors on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68476071/
10 NC: 2023:KHC-K:6555 sufficient room for passage of other vehicles.
Failure to safely negotiate around stopped vehicle substantiated negligence of Tempo driver.
It was submitted that police after due investigation had filed charge sheet against drivers of both vehicles.
It was submitted that failure to produce driving licence of Tempo driver and permitting passengers to travel in goods vehicle was in violation of provisions of M.V. Act and policy conditions.
Therefore, there was attempt to shift entire liability upon Lorry driver.
It was submitted that in facts and circumstances of present nature, at best, it would be appropriate to apportion negligence equally between both drivers.

Insofar as quantum of compensation, it was submitted that on proper consideration,
compensation assessed was just and proper and did not call for enhancement.
17. Shri M. Sudarshan, learned counsel for respondent no.4 - insurer of Tempo sought to justify award.
It was submitted that admittedly Tempo was a - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6555 goods vehicle, in which owner/driver had permitted carriage of passengers.
Since same would be in violation of policy conditions, dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.4 - insurer was justified and no interference would be called for.

18. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgments and awards and also records.
19.

From above submission, while claimants are in appeal challenging dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.4 - insurer, apportionment of contributory negligence between drivers of both vehicles and seeking for enhancement of compensation, insurers seek to sustain award.

Therefore, points that arise for consideration are:
i. Whether dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.4 - insurer of Tempo and fastening liability on owner calls for modification?
- 18 -  NC: 2023:KHC-K:6555  ii.
Whether apportionment of  contributory negligence between driver of Tempo and driver of Lorry, calls for interference?
iii. Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?

Point no.(i):
20. From facts and contentions as narrated above, it would not be in dispute that accident involved two motor vehicles.
Tribunal apportioned negligence to extent of 60% against driver of Tempo and 40% against driver of Lorry.
Said finding is sought to be challenged only by claimants, while insurers accepted said finding.
21. Admittedly, claimants are third parties.

Despite violation of terms and conditions of policy for permitting passengers to travel in goods vehicle, when accident is due to negligence of multiple tort feasors, as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Khenyei's case (supra), claimants would be entitled to proceed and recover entire - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6555 compensation from any one of joint tort feasors.

Further, Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shivaraj v/s Rajendra, reported in (2018) 10 SCC 432, after referring to its earlier decisions in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v/s Swaran Singh, reported in (2004) 3 SCC 297; Mangla Ram v/s Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656; Rani v/s National Insurance Co.
Ltd., reported in (2018) 8 SCC 492 and Manuara Khatun v/s Rajesh Kumar Singh, reported in (2017) 4 SCC 796, held that even in case of gratuitous passengers in goods vehicle, insurer cannot escape liability.

22. In view of above legal position, dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.4 - insurer would be unsustainable.
Consequently, point no.(i) is answered in affirmative as above.
In order to establish occurrence of accident, claimants produced FIR, Complaint, Spot Panchnama, Motor Vehicle Inspectors Reports and Charge sheet as Exhibits-P1 to P7 respectively.
FIR reveals that it is registered based on statements of Shivaji Rathod - inmate of Tempo and drivers of both vehicles recorded by Police Constable in hospital.

Ex . P7-charge sheet is against drivers of both vehicles for offences under Section 279, 337, 338, 304(A), 427 of IPC and Sections 184, 66(1) and 192 of M.V. Act.
24.
Contents of Ex.P4, would reveal that highway was running east to west with twenty-eight feet wide carriageways of two lanes separated by five feet wide median.
It also mention about continues white strip painted three feet from edge of road and broken line in between two lanes.
Accident spot sketch in Ex.P4 reveals that Lorry was parked on left side lane virtually blocking it and there is no mention of any precautionary measures.

12 - 21 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6555 Regulation 15(1) of Rules of the Road Regulations, 1989, prohibit parking of vehicle in such manner as to cause danger, obstruction or undue inconvenience to other road users.
It also mandates that manner of parking to be indicated by any sign board or markings on road.
Therefore, parking of Lorry by its driver on highway would be in violation of law attracting assignment of negligence.

25. Though Exhibits-P5 and P6-MVI reports indicate damage caused to Tempo was on its front side,
while those on Lorry were on right rear side, merely on said basis, no conclusion can be drawn about driver of Tempo attempting to avoid collision by swerving towards right side.
Since accident occurred at 2:00 p.m. during broad day light, some portion of negligence has to be assigned against driver of Tempo also.

Considering above mentioned facts and circumstances, apportionment of 60%
negligence against driver of Tempo would be wholly unsustainable.

It would be appropriate to apportion - 22 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6555 contributory negligence in ratio of 20% against driver of Tempo and 80%
against driver of Lorry.
Point no.(ii) is answered partly in affirmative as above.
Point no.(iii):
26. MFA.no.200051/2018 in MVC.no.1960/2014, claimants - namely wife and three children, have stated that deceased - Yashwant Miraje aged 50 years was earning Rs.12,000/- per month from driving.
But same is not substantiated with specific evidence.
In absence, tribunal assessed it notionally at Rs.5,000/-.
Since notional income for year 2014, adopted for settlement of cases before Lok Adalath is Rs.7,500/-, same has to be considered.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Despite violation of terms and conditions of policy for permitting passengers to travel in goods vehicle, when accident is due to negligence of multiple tort feasors, as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Khenyei's case (supra), claimants would be entitled to proceed and recover entire - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6555 compensation from any one of joint tort feasors.
Further, Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shivaraj v/s Rajendra, reported in (2018) 10 SCC 432, after referring to its earlier decisions in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v/s Swaran Singh, reported in (2004) 3 SCC 297; Mangla Ram v/s Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656; Rani v/s National Insurance Co.
Ltd., reported in (2018) 8 SCC 492 and Manuara Khatun v/s Rajesh Kumar Singh, reported in (2017) 4 SCC 796, held that even in case of gratuitous passengers in goods vehicle, insurer cannot escape liability.
Therefore, parking of Lorry by its driver on highway would be in violation of law attracting assignment of negligence.
Since accident occurred at 2:00 p.m. during broad day light, some portion of negligence has to be assigned against driver of Tempo also.
Considering above mentioned facts and circumstances, apportionment of 60%
negligence against driver of Tempo would be wholly unsustainable.
But same is not substantiated with specific evidence.
